description.text: Hyatt Hotels Corporation is a global hospitality company with widely recognized, industry-leading brands and a tradition of innovation developed over our almost 70-year history. Hyatt's portfolio of properties consists of full service hotels and resorts, select service hotels, all-inclusive resorts, and other properties, including timeshare, fractional, and other forms of residential and vacation units. We also offer distribution and destination management services through ALG Vacations and distribution services through Mr & Mrs Smith, a boutique and luxury global travel platform. On June 17, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Playa Hotels & Resorts N.V. ("Playa Hotels" or the "Playa Hotels Acquisition"), a leading owner, operator, and developer of all-inclusive resorts in Mexico, the Dominican Republic, and Jamaica. At December 31, 2025, our hotel portfolio consisted of 1,528 hotels and all-inclusive resorts (372,763 rooms). See Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Overview" for a breakdown of our portfolio. Our colleagues and hotel general managers are supported by our regional management teams, located in cities around the world, and our executive management team, headquartered in Chicago. Our offering includes brands across five distinct portfolios.

about.description_short: Hyatt Hotels Corporation, headquartered in Chicago, is a leading global hospitality company guided by its purpose - to care for people so they can be their best. As of June 30, 2026, the Company's portfolio included more than 1,500 hotels and all-inclusive properties in 83 countries across six continents.

employees.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we had approximately 242,000 colleagues working at our corporate and regional offices, our managed, franchised, owned, and leased properties, the Bahia Principe Hotels & Resorts properties that are managed by a consolidated hospitality venture, and the Unlimited Vacation Club business that we manage.

analysis_md:
# H — Hyatt Hotels Corp
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-16. Price $169.13 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap (est) $16.153B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Global lodging company skewed to luxury, lifestyle, and all-inclusive: managed/franchised fee business plus a shrinking owned/leased estate, World of Hyatt loyalty, and distribution (ALG Vacations, Mr & Mrs Smith). The defining 2025 event was the Playa Hotels acquisition (June 2025) followed by the sale of the entire Playa real estate portfolio for $2.0B, closed December 30, 2025, with 50-year management agreements retained on the sold resorts — i.e., Hyatt bought the fee contracts and briefly owned the real estate in between. Q2 2026 prints (via search of the Q2 2026 release): comparable system-wide RevPAR +5.9%, gross fees $324M (+7.8%), Adjusted EBITDA $297M, net rooms growth 3.9% (4.4% excluding Playa rooms removed in H2 2025), pipeline ~154,000 rooms (+10.0%), FY2026 RevPAR guidance 3.5–4.5% and net rooms growth ~6%.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $379,000,000; capex $220,000,000; SBC $74,000,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $85,000,000 = $0.89/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $0.89, latest FY OE total $85.0M)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $5,000,000 total in FY2025 (financials_history.csv) — even weaker than the conservative figure; in FY2024 the two definitions ran the other way (conservative $399,000,000 vs maintenance $682,000,000). Neither single year is a run rate for this company.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years on the conservative definition, but the range is extreme: OE/share was $3.70 (2022), $4.89 (2023), $3.90 (2024), $0.89 (2025), and -$7.51 in 2020 (all financials_history.csv).
- Net debt $3.491B (key_numbers.md); lease liabilities $278,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json).

**TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct, run for STALE_FY — quoted in full, NOT used as the base):**
- OCF: FY $379,000,000 − prior YTD $86,000,000 + current YTD $150,000,000 = **TTM $443,000,000**
- Capex: FY $220,000,000 − prior YTD $74,000,000 + current YTD $45,000,000 = **TTM $191,000,000**
- SBC: FY $74,000,000 − prior YTD $46,000,000 + current YTD $45,000,000 = **TTM $73,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **96,732,008**
- **TTM OE total $179,000,000 → TTM OE/share $1.85**

**Base used = normalized 3-yr median OE/share $3.90** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The latest FY and the TTM are both distorted down by the same transient: both windows contain the period when Hyatt owned the Playa real estate it had already agreed to sell. The FY2025 release decomposition (via search) shows consolidated OCF $379M = Hyatt ex-Playa $558M plus Playa -$179M, and consolidated capex $220M = ex-Playa $148M plus Playa $72M, with $198M of Playa acquisition costs also running through the year. That ownership period ended December 30, 2025; the resorts now contribute fees under 50-year contracts instead of owned drag. The median ($3.90, earned pre-Playa in 2023–24) is the least-distorted base — and it is not flattering versus forward evidence: FY2026 guidance in the Q4 2025 presentation (via search) implies OCF of $628–678M against capex of $135M, a run rate above the TTM print. The TTM $1.85 is retained as bear-side evidence in the method range below.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: Strong luxury/lifestyle brands and World of Hyatt — the highest-value major hotel loyalty currency — plus long-dated management contracts (50-year terms on the sold Playa resorts) and a 154,000-room pipeline, but subscale at ~1,400-1,500 properties vs Marriott/Hilton at 8,000-9,000+, no filed ROIC/gross-margin series in fundamentals.json (operating income untagged, roic_proxy null), and a volatile, thin OE record (negative in 2020, $0.89/share in 2025) that does not evidence returns well above cost of capital through a cycle.
- FOR: World of Hyatt loyalty — highest-value major hotel points currency, high-end guest base; luxury/lifestyle brand portfolio (Park Hyatt, Alila, Inclusive Collection) skewed to high-value guests; long-dated fee contracts — 50-year management agreements on the Playa resorts sold in Dec 2025; pipeline ~154,000 rooms (+10% YoY) and net rooms growth ~4-6% supporting fee growth.
- AGAINST: Subscale network (~1,400-1,500 properties) vs Marriott/Hilton at 8,000-9,000+ — weaker owner distribution and loyalty network effects; no evidenced high ROIC (roic_proxy and gross margin are null in fundamentals.json — operating income is not tagged, so neither series exists in the computed outputs); cyclical lodging demand — revenue fell from $5,020M (2019) to $2,066M (2020); leverage — net debt $3,491M is 9.4x normalized OE (flag basis; diagnostics in key_numbers.md: 9.38x).
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.
- On the required ROIC/margin evidence: fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy series and no gross-margin series for Hyatt (both null, because no operating-income tag is filed in the engine's candidate set). There is therefore no computed ROIC history to quote, and a moat above 6 on this record would be assertion, not evidence — the OE record above is the observable return history, and it is thin and volatile.

## DCF — final run (engine 5.4.0)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's blended growth is 11.58% (g_base 11.58%), but its components do not describe the current business — rev CAGR 5y 28.01% is a COVID-rebound artifact (2020 revenue was the $2,066M trough), OE/share CAGR 2y is -57.32%, and the revenue components carry a +4.96pp buyback adjustment (share count CAGR -4.96%). The prints that mean something — latest rev YoY 6.81%, rev CAGR 3y 6.42%, TTM revenue YoY +5.8% (fundamentals.json), Q2 2026 RevPAR +5.9% and gross fees +7.8%, FY2026 guidance of RevPAR 3.5–4.5% with net rooms growth ~6% — center on ~6%. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (-0.116 / -0.086 / -0.056 / -0.026 / +0.014 vs g_base) to -0.0% / 3.0% / **6.0%** / 9.0% / 13.0%. Probabilities 15/25/30/20/10 (bear-or-worse widened to 40% for OE_VOLATILE and HIGH_NET_DEBT); OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 (defaults). Price $169.13.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -0.0% | 0.75 | Lodging cycle turns; RevPAR falls, levered OE compresses | $21.57 | 4.04% |
| Bear | 25% | 3.0% | 0.90 | RevPAR at the low end of guide, slow rooms growth | $29.33 | 4.68% |
| Base | 30% | 6.0% | 1.00 | Guide delivered: RevPAR ~4% + rooms ~6%, fees compounding | $36.91 | 5.33% |
| Bull | 20% | 9.0% | 1.10 | Asset-light mix shift lifts OE faster than revenue; buybacks help | $45.97 | 6.10% |
| Super bull | 10% | 13.0% | 1.25 | Fee growth re-accelerates, owned drag fully exits, Playa fees scale | $61.56 | 7.40% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $36.99 (-78.1% vs price), IV@12% $49.21, IV@10% $62.85, weighted IRR 5.35%, base-case IRR 5.33%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear tier D, bull tier D — every scenario is individually Tier D). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 2.30%, terminal value 18.9% of IV@15%, scenario spread 2.85x, net debt 9.38x normalized OE, 9.5 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path, key_numbers.md): 15% at $36.99 · 20% at $26.02 · 25% at $19.99.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago): ttm.py was run and its full legs are quoted above (TTM OE/share $1.85, saved to ttm.json). The TTM base was *not* adopted — see BASE_DIVERGENCE; the median base is used, with the TTM figure disclosed as bear-side evidence. Current-quarter evidence (Q2 2026 RevPAR, fees, guidance) is reflected in the scenario starts instead.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 5.0%/yr): confirmed (share count CAGR -4.96%, growth adj 4.96% in key_numbers.md) and already credited via the growth adjustment inside the blend — not double-counted. Note the caveat: at $169.13 against a $36.99 weighted IV@15%, buybacks retire stock far above this model's intrinsic value, which destroys rather than creates per-share value at this price.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs): two real breaks, both identified. (1) COVID: revenue $5,020M (2019) → $2,066M (2020) → $5,891M (2022) in financials_history.csv — the 28.01% 5-yr revenue CAGR straddles the trough and was not trusted; growth was set from 3-yr CAGR, latest YoY, TTM, and guidance instead. (2) Playa: acquired June 2025, real estate sold December 30, 2025 for $2.0B with 50-year management contracts — the OE history straddles a brief owned-resort period that no longer exists; handled under BASE_DIVERGENCE by using the pre-Playa median.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x): real and structural for a lodging company with owned exposure — $3.70 / $4.89 / $3.90 / $0.89 across 2022–25 and -$7.51 in 2020 (financials_history.csv). - **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): explained year by year from the filed history and releases. 2024: net income $1,296,000,000 vs OCF $633,000,000 — net income contains $1,245M of gains on sales of real estate (Q4 2024 release reconciliation, via search), which are investing, not operating, cash; the OCF-based conservative OE is unaffected by the gain. 2023: net income $220,000,000 vs OCF $800,000,000 — non-cash D&A of $397,000,000 (financials_history.csv) plus working-capital timing. 2025: net income -$52,000,000 vs OCF $379,000,000 — D&A of $325,000,000, asset impairments and Playa transaction/integration costs depress net income, while OCF itself was dragged by Playa's -$179M operating cash flow (release decomposition, via search). In all three years the divergence sits in non-cash or investing items; the OCF-based OE series used throughout is the clean one.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range, and here it does not save the stock: on the TTM base ($1.85/share) the value would be roughly half the headline; on the median base actually used, weighted IV@15% is $36.99; even the super-bull scenario (13.0% growth start, 1.25x OE) yields only a 7.40% IRR and an IV@15% of $61.56 — still 64% below the $169.13 price. Every defensible method lands in Tier D.
- Quality is real but priced: the asset-light direction is genuine (Playa real estate exited, 50-year fee contracts kept, pipeline +10%), World of Hyatt is the most valuable major loyalty currency, and Q2 2026 fee growth of +7.8% is a good print. None of that bridges a 2.30% OE yield at this price — the buyer at $169.13 is paying for a fee-compounder outcome the filed OE history has not yet produced.
- What would change the verdict: several years of post-Playa filed OE/share at or above the $3.90 median with the leverage paid down, or a price anywhere near the hurdle levels. On this model the stock clears 15% only below ~$36.99.
- Risks to this (short-side) verdict: a sustained RevPAR upcycle plus faster buybacks at lower prices, further asset sales at large gains recycled into buybacks, or the market continuing to price Hyatt on Adjusted EBITDA (~$1.1–1.2B guided) rather than owner's earnings — the gap between those two measures (D&A, SBC, and the owned-estate capex) is exactly what this sweep refuses to ignore.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 5.35% on the final inputs; bear tier D, bull tier D, super-bull IRR 7.40% — no scenario reaches 10%)
- Confidence: **Low** (base distortion from the Playa window, OE volatility, and 9.4x leverage; the tier itself is robust — it is D on every base and every scenario)
- One-liner: Quality lodging franchisor in an asset-light transition, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $169.13: weighted IRR 5.35%, weighted IV@15% $36.99, and even the super-bull case (7.40% IRR) is Tier D; clears 15% only below ~$36.99.
